observations: Q2 2026 revenue was $3.4B, up 10.9% year over year; operating income was $210M and operating margin 6.1% versus $163M and 5.3% a year earlier.
HII raised FY26 shipbuilding revenue guidance to $10.2B-$10.4B and raised the low end of shipbuilding operating-margin guidance while reaffirming free-cash-flow outlook.
Q2 operating cash flow was negative $31M and free cash flow negative $150M versus positive $823M and $730M respectively a year earlier.
Six-month operating cash use was $421M versus $428M provided in the prior-year period; the 10-Q attributes the swing primarily to unfavorable trade working-capital timing across programs.
Q2 awards were $6.7B and backlog was $57.3B at June 30, 2026.
Ingalls Q2 revenue increased 17% year over year to $845M, driven primarily by higher amphibious-assault-ship volume, while segment margin was 6.9% versus 7.5%.
risks: Strong revenue/margin improvement coexists with materially weaker cash conversion; working-capital timing remains an execution variable.
Backlog and awards provide demand visibility but do not by themselves prove schedule, labor, supplier or cash-conversion execution.
contradictions: Income-statement momentum improved while quarterly and first-half operating cash flow deteriorated sharply year over year; this is a real operating/cash-conversion tension rather than evidence to average away.
unknowns: Whether the working-capital cash outflow reverses on management's expected schedule.
Realized economics of the 15% shipbuilding-throughput improvement objective.
Scout does not set Alpha numeric factor values, risk, confidence or final score.
recommendation: Use the SEC-filed Q2/10-Q figures as source-addressed operating evidence for financial momentum and risk calibration. Preserve the cash-conversion tension explicitly when Alpha constructs numeric factors and confidence.
